reasons: Both answers recommend embedding-based dynamic few-shot with diversification and contrast pairs, rewritten boundary descriptions, cost analysis of the 600M tokens/day, and a held-out per-category evaluation. B additionally tells the user to put the most similar examples closest to the ticket, adds a retrieval recall@k check with a BM25 hybrid fallback, and covers the cache warm-rate, prompt injection and two-stage classification. A's k of 6-10 fits the rubric range more tightly than B's 10-15, and its warning about small-sample noise is a good point, but B's extra practical checks give it a slight edge overall.
